topics.name: Constraint-aware sequential decision-making
topics.summary: These studies combine constraint solvers, structured reinforcement learning, Bayesian exploration, and risk-sensitive policy optimization for decisions made with limited feedback, uncertain outcomes, or costly search. Their applications emphasize preserving feasibility, robustness, and useful performance while reducing exploration effort.

topics.name: Fairness and calibration under biased feedback
topics.summary: These papers analyze learning when rewards, labels, or outcomes are selectively observed, delayed, soft, or unevenly distributed. Propensity adjustments, fairness guarantees, and calibration methods are used to make predictions and decisions more reliable under realistic feedback problems.

topics.name: Recommender systems, personalization, and digital commerce
topics.summary: Recommendation systems model user intent, durable behavior, controllability, and marketplace context rather than optimizing immediate clicks alone. The papers use causal or temporal representations, federated adaptation, catalog agents, and preference-aware interaction to improve ranking quality and user outcomes.

topics.name: Autonomous vehicle planning, control, and perception
topics.summary: Vehicle autonomy is addressed through predictive control, probabilistic planning, information-aware sensing, and temporal 3D perception. Experiments span racing, intersections, aerial vehicles, heavy trucks, and driving scenes, with recurring attention to collision risk, tracking limits, localization, and closed-loop behavior.

topics.name: Safe adaptive control and generative control
topics.summary: These works impose stability or safety structure on learned controllers and stochastic generators. Barrier functions, Lyapunov conditions, adaptive dynamics, and entropy-based guidance support reliable behavior despite changing system parameters, constrained trajectories, or sampling-time uncertainty.

topics.name: Mobile, marine, and language-guided robot navigation
topics.summary: Robot mobility studies combine terrain-aware sensing, learned locomotion, language grounding, active search, and configuration-dependent dynamics. Applications include quadrupeds, assistive vehicles, underwater platforms, surface craft, and household robots operating with incomplete maps or changing conditions.

topics.name: Robot manipulation, deformables, and contact
topics.summary: Manipulation systems learn from demonstrations, tactile or visual feedback, simulation corrections, and multimodal action representations. Across clutter, deformable objects, contact events, uncertainty, and long-horizon tasks, the methods emphasize recovery, physical modeling, data efficiency, and transfer across embodiments.

topics.name: Space robotics and autonomous spacecraft servicing
topics.summary: The papers develop model-free spacecraft pose estimation and decentralized repair of modular structures. Learned geometric matching and local stress-based coordination reduce reliance on prior vehicle models, external markers, or centralized planning during servicing operations.

topics.name: Multi-robot mapping, localization, and exploration
topics.summary: These systems improve robot teams and autonomous platforms through fast collision checking, loop-closure correction, cooperative localization, fiducial sensing, and transferable visual dynamics. Shared maps and active viewpoint selection help balance coverage, reconstruction quality, and execution cost.

topics.name: 3D geometric vision and content generation
topics.summary: Geometric vision methods use surface-aware fields, implicit occupancy, Gaussian representations, structured shape spaces, and diffusion-based synthesis. The applications range from scene reconstruction to articulated human modeling and garment editing, with emphasis on topology, thin structures, correspondence, and editable output.

topics.name: Video generation, understanding, and rendering
topics.summary: Video systems condition synthesis on music, references, keyframes, or language while modeling temporal structure and identity. Other contributions accelerate rendering and representation learning through sparse geometry, frozen encoders, salient moments, and specialized hardware execution, with evaluations targeting coherence and controllability.

topics.name: Image and video restoration with physical priors
topics.summary: Restoration methods handle rain, darkness, weather changes, microscopy depth, and indoor illumination by separating signal components or embedding imaging physics. Unpaired diffusion, event information, confidence-aware fusion, and focus variation are used to preserve structure while improving downstream visual perception.

topics.name: Visual recognition, grounding, and spatial representations
topics.summary: Fine-grained recognition benefits from local regions, motion, relational cues, spatial token organization, and instance-specific descriptions. The studies cover occlusion, incremental categories, scene text, human-object interaction, medical concepts, and biologically arranged inputs, showing limits of global embeddings.

topics.name: Multimodal reasoning and incomplete sensing
topics.summary: Cross-modal fusion is used to recover information missing from degraded inputs and to solve tasks requiring visual comparison or quantitative analysis. Results across image-text classification and physics-oriented benchmarks show that grounding and multi-step visual reasoning remain harder than text-only inference.

topics.name: World models and interactive simulation
topics.summary: Latent predictive models are tested for forecasting, state representation, synchronized scene editing, and long-horizon interaction. Earth observation, driving, video, games, and code environments reveal that controllable state transitions and rollout behavior matter more than isolated next-step accuracy.

topics.name: Efficient transformers and multimodal inference
topics.summary: Transformer efficiency is improved through recurrent block reuse, token selection, ternary factorization, distillation, pruning, and graph compilation. Across language, vision, and retrieval workloads, the methods trade redundant computation for lower latency, memory use, or deployment cost while retaining task quality.

topics.name: Neural plasticity, adaptive computation, and sparse learning
topics.summary: These studies reduce update cost or exploit internal training structure through local error transport, small parameter changes, adaptive depth, attention statistics, and sparse-subnetwork discovery. The recurring objective is to preserve useful representations while making learning and inference more selective.

topics.name: LLM post-training, self-distillation, and personalization
topics.summary: Language-model adaptation is treated as a resource allocation problem involving rollout search, feedback quality, token-level supervision, agreement signals, and client heterogeneity. Reinforcement learning, self-distillation, federated updates, and instruction tuning are compared for stable gains under limited compute or data.

topics.name: Agent orchestration, memory, skills, and test-time search
topics.summary: Agent frameworks represent workflows as graphs and use learned controllers to select tools, retrieve memories, reuse skills, repair plans, or branch execution. Experience stores, hierarchical abilities, parallel alternatives, and lightweight routing reduce redundant trials and improve performance on data and software tasks.

topics.name: Agent safety, evaluation, reliability, and governance
topics.summary: These papers develop audits, benchmarks, permissions, intervention policies, confidence tests, and execution records for agents acting through tools. They examine adversarial behavior, evaluator reliability, calibration, instruction conflicts, data leakage, and accountability, arguing that deployment claims require application-specific evidence and traceable actions.

topics.name: Generative model steering, constraints, and adversarial testing
topics.summary: Generative systems are redirected or stress-tested with example-based steering, indirect concept links, autonomous red-team data, executable checks, citation tests, fuzzing, and constraint-aware training. These methods expose hidden failures and improve control when static prompts or aggregate quality scores are insufficient.

topics.name: Privacy leakage and distribution shift in generative AI
topics.summary: The studies show that synthetic data and stylistic shifts can alter privacy exposure and detector reliability. Membership inference, memorization analysis, adversarial examples, and dataset-level indicators are used to identify risks that remain hidden when evaluation stays close to the training distribution.

topics.name: Verified program synthesis and coding agents
topics.summary: Code-generating systems are improved with compiler feedback, validator diagnostics, targeted reasoning repair, repository-level evaluation, continual task streams, and verifier-aware decoding. These methods favor incremental correction and structural validity over repeated unconstrained generation, including for quantum circuits.

topics.name: Human-centered evaluation and applied language models
topics.summary: Applied language models are assessed with expert judgments and operational measures rather than accuracy alone. Educational studies examine question quality and reasoning demands, while agricultural deployment work tracks compliance, usefulness, latency, workload, and the role of human supervision.

topics.name: Human-AI interaction, adoption, and alignment
topics.summary: These studies examine how people rely on AI advice, adapt their expectations, and negotiate responsibility in workplaces and ongoing interaction. Abstention, user-context uncertainty, trajectory-level collaboration, and longitudinal adoption evidence support assistants that clarify limits and complement human judgment.

topics.name: Speech, affective computing, and multimodal social interaction
topics.summary: Speech and affect systems combine prosody, acoustic timing, facial behavior, language, identity, and conversational context. The datasets and models address emotion, ambivalence, group engagement, speaker variation, and missing modalities, with temporal fusion and normalization repeatedly improving robustness.

topics.name: Fine-grained human activity and gesture recognition
topics.summary: Action-recognition methods focus on subtle motion and localized body changes that static appearance can obscure. Higher-order temporal relations, anatomy-aware features, and motion-sensitive tokenization are evaluated on manipulation, micro-gesture, and activity video benchmarks.

topics.name: Low-resource language and document understanding
topics.summary: Low-resource language systems address glossing, captioning, multilingual adaptation, document reformulation, OCR, and handwritten text. Compact architectures, synthetic-real training mixtures, parameter composition, retrieval of broader context, and deployment-oriented robustness are recurring strategies.

topics.name: Retrieval-augmented and knowledge-grounded clinical QA
topics.summary: Search and clinical question-answering systems combine semantic retrieval with interaction history, selective re-search, process-level feedback, and structured biomedical evidence. Region-aware and graph-based grounding helps reduce omitted findings and unsupported relationships in answers and reports.

topics.name: Medical imaging adaptation, reconstruction, and segmentation
topics.summary: Medical vision methods cope with site variation, missing annotations, sparse CT measurements, and difficult boundaries through federated training, latent experts, triplane representations, implicit reconstruction, language prompts, and lightweight adaptation. The shared goal is reliable spatial prediction with reduced data or memory requirements.

topics.name: Multimodal clinical prediction and decision support
topics.summary: Clinical prediction systems fuse imaging, metadata, longitudinal records, ECG signals, and multimodal language supervision to characterize disease and forecast risk. Their evaluations emphasize temporal sparsity, clinically meaningful regions or subdomains, interactive reasoning, and generalization beyond fixed-label classification.

topics.name: Trustworthy medical AI and explainability
topics.summary: Medical AI reliability is assessed with counterfactual interventions, calibrated uncertainty, morphology-based explanations, leakage checks, and explicit attribution assumptions. The studies ask whether highlighted evidence changes predictions, reflects clinical structure, and supports appropriate deferral rather than merely improving a headline score.

topics.name: Scientific machine learning for PDEs and inverse problems
topics.summary: Neural and probabilistic solvers for PDEs, inverse problems, and material simulation incorporate operators, spectral structure, measurement consistency, recurrent surrogates, or learned bases. These inductive biases improve approximation in high-dimensional or ill-posed settings, although uncertainty and model mismatch remain central concerns.

topics.name: AI-assisted scientific discovery
topics.summary: Scientific agents combine retrieval with causal analogies, mechanistic equation construction, derivation checks, experiments, expert review, and closed-loop intervention. The recurring finding is that explicit structure and verification are needed for useful discovery beyond surface similarity or unconstrained numerical fitting.

topics.name: Graph and network learning under structural variation
topics.summary: Graph methods recover latent organization, detect communities, and handle changes in topology or label balance. Gauge-aware potentials, entropy-based updates, shared multi-task encoders, importance sampling, and signal-space anomaly detection are used to improve stability across evolving or heterogeneous networks.

topics.name: Quantum and topology-aware machine learning
topics.summary: These studies encode molecular connectivity, clique structure, or higher-order topology into quantum and hybrid learning systems. Comparisons with classical baselines indicate that structural inductive bias can improve discrimination or data efficiency, especially when samples are represented by relations rather than flat vectors.

topics.name: Geometric learning for molecular structure and dynamics
topics.summary: Geometric molecular models use symmetry-aware attention, spatial features, and trajectory representations to predict properties and emulate long biological dynamics. Their evaluations emphasize robustness to noisy conformations and the preservation of physically meaningful relationships across time and three-dimensional structure.

topics.name: Operational anomaly detection and data quality
topics.summary: Anomaly systems for finance, industrial inspection, and wind-farm telemetry address false alarms, operating-mode mixtures, boundary effects, and weak labels. Explainable scores, normality prototypes, and clustering-based filtering improve localization and dataset quality while retaining a role for calibration and expert review.

topics.name: Financial forecasting and systemic risk
topics.summary: These papers apply neural operators, horizon-specific predictors, graph counterfactuals, and stochastic-process models to markets and contagion. Applications include hedging, stock forecasting, cascade prevention, and event-contract pricing, with calibration and time-to-expiry effects shaping reported reliability.

topics.name: Mechanism design and digital markets
topics.summary: Automated delegation and marketplace mechanisms are studied through regret analysis, randomized advertising experiments, contract design, and probability calibration. The results examine how proxies, ad load, reports, and event prices alter incentives, truthful information, and user welfare.

topics.name: Algorithmic cooperation and social simulation
topics.summary: Repeated-agent interaction and human-bot organization are modeled with stochastic learning, reputation aggregation, rule-based simulation, language-model agents, and digital twins. The papers connect durable cooperation to exploration, memory, role differentiation, and the way contributions are judged across contexts.

topics.name: Automated analog circuit design
topics.summary: Analog design automation combines reinforcement learning, evolutionary search, language-model synthesis, templates, simulation checks, and speciation over circuit topologies. These methods address expensive design spaces by reusing strong configurations and enforcing electrical or structural validity during exploration.

topics.name: Human-centered robot learning and social dialogue
topics.summary: Human signals and social context are incorporated into robot learning through offline brain measurements, visual-language perception, and dialogue modeling. The studies consider noisy observations, response latency, and deployment constraints while seeking more responsive control and richer interaction.

topics.name: Learned image and video compression
topics.summary: Neural codecs allocate capacity across temporal structure, frame content, bitrate, and expert subnetworks. State-space prediction, sparse specialization, and adaptive depth improve rate-distortion behavior without requiring a separate full model for every operating point.

topics.name: Certified robustness and neural verification
topics.summary: These works study formal guarantees for neural networks under perturbations and parameter uncertainty. Complexity results clarify limits of exact verification, while broader analyses organize Lipschitz bounds, estimation procedures, regularization, and certification strategies for robust deployment.

topics.name: Active learning for bioacoustic detection
topics.summary: Budgeted bioacoustic labeling is improved by selecting diverse and informative audio batches under severe class imbalance. Embedding-space coverage, soft disagreement weighting, greedy volume objectives, and facility-location criteria help discover rare calls with fewer annotations.

topics.name: Artificial intelligence for art analysis and retrieval
topics.summary: Multimodal art systems model relations among visual features, text, and art-historical context rather than relying only on global similarity. Retrieval embeddings and expert-centered evaluation reveal gains in contextual matching alongside persistent calibration and ranking weaknesses in automated assessment.
